text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
American historian and author of short stories including "Rip Van Winkle", WASHINGTON IRVING, was born in 1783.

The "Father of Australian wheat", WILLIAM FARRER, who came to Australia in 1870 and began experimenting with cross-pollinating wheat, was born in 1845 in England. He developed more than 300 varieties of wheat while working on a property near Queanbeyan, including some that could withstand drought.
The man who brought author FRANK HARDY fame and controversy was sports promoter JOHN WREN, who was born in 1871.In "Power Without Glory", HARDY based his character of John West on JOHN WREN SENIOR.
English author DAISY ASHFORD, who wrote "The Young Visitors" at the age of 9, was born in 1881.
American publisher HENRY LUCE, who founded "TIME", "LIFE" and "FORTUNE" magazines, was born in 1898.
American method-actor MARLON BRANDO, who won Oscars for "On The Waterfront" and "The Godfather", was born in 1924.

American actress and singer DORIS DAY was born in 1924. Her real name was DORIS VON KAPPELHOFF. She initially wanted to be a dancer but injured her legs and then turned to singing. She began her career in the 1930s with BARNEY RAPP's band and appeared with a succession of bands. DORIS began

recording under her own name in 1947. She had hits with "Love Somebody" (1948), "It's Magic" (1948), "A Guy Is A Guy" (1952) and "Whatever Will Be Will Be (Que Sera Sera)" (1952). She made a successful transition to movies and her films included "Pillow Talk" (1959), "Midnight Lace" (1960) and "A Touch Of Mink" (1961).
German statesman HELMUT KOHL, twice elected Chancellor, was born in 1930.

US singer WAYNE NEWTON was born in 1942. He appeared on the JACKIE GLEASON television programme in 1962. His first hit was "Danke Schon" (1963) and his biggest hit was in 1972 with "Daddy Don't You Walk So Fast".

American comedian and actor EDDIE MURPHY was born in 1961. His first hit was "Party All The Time" (1985) and was written and produced by RICK JAMES. His best known films include "Beverly Hills Cop", "48 Hours" and "The Golden Child".
** EVENTS **
1862 : British explorer SIR JAMES CLARK ROSS, who gave
his name to Ross Barrier, Ross Island and Ross Sea, Antarctica, died.
1882 : American gangster JESSE JAMES (THOMAS HOWARD) was
gunned-down at his home in St Joseph, Missouri. JAMES was killed by a new member of his gang BOB FORD, who allegedly shot him in the back of the head while he was straightening a picture frame.
1897 : German composer JOHANNES BRAHMS died.
1917 : VLADIMIR ILICH LENIN returned to Moscow from
exile, saying "Any Cook should be able to run the country".
1922 : JOSEPH STALIN was appointed General Secretary of
the Communist Party in Russia.
1936 : German-born carpenter BRUNO HAUPTMANN went to the
electric chair for the kidnap and murder of the 20-month old baby son of aviation hero CHARLES LINDBERGH and his wife ANNE.
1943 : Tensions between American and New Zealand

servicemen erupted in violence in Auckland and Wellington. The Kiwis, like their Australian counterparts, didn't take to kindly to the US soldiers who were taking out their girlfriends. A series of violent brawls started between soldiers from the deep south and Maori troops. Wellington's Manners Street was badly damaged.
1969 : JIM MORRISON from the "Doors" pop group was

arrested by the FBI in Los Angeles and charged with 'fleeing interstate to avoid prosecution'. He had been charged with "lewd and lascivious behaviour in public" at a concert in Miami the month before.
1982 : JOHN CAIN became the first Labor Premier of
Victoria in 27 years, since the Labor Administration of his Father.
1982 : While Argentina celebrated its invasion of the
Falkland Islands, Britain demanded immediate withdrawal.
1987 : Jewellery belonging to the late DUCHESS OF WINDSOR

(WALLIS SIMPSON, who died a year earlier) went up for auction in Geneva, fetching more than 62 million dollars. The money raised went to medical research, while some of the prominent buyers of the royal jewellery included ELIZABETH TAYLOR and JOAN COLLINS.
1991 : Author GRAHAM GREENE died at the age of 86.
